page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, alongside a 35 MB L3 cache. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 154 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates that the D4ds_v4 delivers moderate single-core performance but shows limitations under multi-core and memory-intensive workloads. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 24.28 GB/sec and Geekbench single-core execution with a score of 1277.0 fall within average ranges. However, multi-threaded operations and raw computational throughput are generally weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 3678.27 and a Passmark CPU score of 4387.87. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block uncached reads and writes measuring 27.12 GB/sec and 21.12 GB/sec respectively.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, which provides a standard general-purpose profile. The inclusion of a local 154 GB SSD adds value for workloads requiring fast temporary storage without incurring extra disk costs. Given its performance profile, the D4ds_v4 is best suited for general-purpose workloads, light web serving, text processing, and basic database operations that do not require high multi-threaded CPU scaling or extreme memory bandwidth.
